fact_text: The price-to-earnings ratio compares a share price with expected future earnings; a stock is undervalued when earnings are expected to rise and the price has not reflected it, and overvalued when the reverse holds.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How to Tell if a Company is Undervalued or Overvalued | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-22)

fact_text: Banks are usually valued on price to book value, which compares the share price with net asset value (assets minus liabilities).
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How to Tell if a Company is Undervalued or Overvalued | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-22)

fact_text: Intrinsic value is a company's true worth based on its ability to generate consistent income and cash flow, which together make the balance sheet strong.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How to Tell if a Company is Undervalued or Overvalued | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-22)

fact_text: Financial strength is judged from three statements together: the balance sheet, the income statement and the cash flow statement.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How to Tell if a Company is Undervalued or Overvalued | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-22)

fact_text: Cyclical sectors such as construction, manufacturing, chemicals and infrastructure development track the economic cycle, while utilities, food and tobacco are non-cyclical.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How to Tell if a Company is Undervalued or Overvalued | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-22)

fact_text: The presenter argued that falling inflation and interest rates lift consumer spending and company sales, while high inflation and rates slow spending and the economy.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How to Tell if a Company is Undervalued or Overvalued | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-22)

fact_text: Businesses run on credit, so late payments from customers squeeze cash flow; if this lasts, companies borrow more, and high interest rates make it worse.
